convertibility_reason: Uses custom indicator ColorJFatl_Digit via iCustom, neural network (3-layer perceptron) for signal filtering, and complex money management (MMRec) with deposit fraction sizing. The JFatl indicator is not a built-in MT5 indicator - it combines JMA smoothing with FATL digital filter coefficients, requiring custom indicator porting or reimplementation.

derived_values.name: NN3 perceptron output
derived_values.formula: sigmoid(W3 * sigmoid(W2 * sigmoid(W1 * inputs + B1) + B2) + B3)

other_exits: Opposite signal closes current position before opening new one
NN3 neural network can veto signal preventing entry but does not independently close positions

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMRec mode: negative input value = fixed lots at abs(value); positive input value = fraction of free margin for position sizing. The 'Recommended' preset uses deposit fraction with 10% of free margin.

custom_logic_notes: The NN3 (3-layer neural network perceptron) acts as a signal filter. It takes market state inputs (price changes, indicator readings) and produces a binary go/no-go decision. A trade signal from the JFatl crossover is only executed if the NN3 output confirms the direction. The ColorJFatl_Digit indicator uses FATL digital filter coefficients (pre-computed as a weighted sum of 39 previous closes) combined with JMA adaptive smoothing. The 'Digit' variant applies an automatic 10x multiplier on SL/TP values when running on 5-digit brokers (or when _Point < 0.001), so input pip values remain consistent regardless of broker digit configuration. The MMRec money management calculates lot size as: lot = (FreeMargin * MMFraction) / (ContractSize * StopLevel_Points * PointValue), clamped to broker min/max lot constraints.
python_conversion_notes: Major challenges: (1) ColorJFatl_Digit custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python - requires FATL digital filter coefficient table (39 weights) plus JMA adaptive smoothing algorithm. This is non-trivial as JMA is proprietary Jurik smoothing. (2) NN3 perceptron weights are typically pre-trained and hardcoded in the EA - these must be extracted from the .mq5 source. Without the binary source being readable, exact weights cannot be determined. (3) The digit adjustment logic (10x for 5-digit brokers) must be handled in Python by checking price decimal places. (4) MMRec lot calculation requires live margin info which differs between backtest engines - consider using fixed fractional sizing as approximation. (5) Recommend re-implementing JFatl as a combination of scipy/numpy digital filter (FATL coefficients) + adaptive smoothing approximation (e.g., Kaufman AMA or T3 as JMA proxy). (6) Signal logic uses [1] previous bar values for crossover detection - ensure Python implementation uses same shift semantics.
